newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian chemical plant Chimko to be sold soon.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian chemical plant Chimko to be sold soon.

text.p: A 57-percent stake of Bulgaria's chemical fertiliser producer Chimko can be sold in 2-3 months and big strategic firms are bidding for it, plant officials said on Wednesday.

"There are no legal, financial or organisational problems to hinder the plant's partial sale in two-three months," Chimko spokeswoman Silvia Nakova quoted the plant's executive director Kiril Petkov as saying.
Nakova said telephone offers for buying the stake were expected until March 15.

She said the plant, which was stabilising its finances, last year had a pre-tax profit of $68 million and its taxes were $37 million. The revenue figure included $155 million from export sales, she said.

The Vratsa-based plant, which imports 64 percent of its raw materials and exports 92 percent of its products, last year produced 791,000 tonnes of carbamide, 532,000 tonnes of ammonia and 2.8 million cubic metres of argon.
Chimko has 20 installations, including those for reforming, carbamide, carbon sulphide, carbon dioxide and a catalytic installation.
Investments for the modernisation of the plant include $15 million for a new water installation, which chemically purifies used water.

Last year the plant set up a joint venture with Frankfurt-based Messer Grieshelm GmbH, a subsidiary of Germany's Hoechst, to distribute industrial gases in the region. Chimko has 49 percent and the Germans have the remaining stake.
